title: PathValidation.ValidateLogDir does not resolve symlinks/junctions — LACERTE_DEBUG_LOG_PATH allowlist bypassable via reparse point under %TEMP%
userOrOpsImpact: An attacker who can create a reparse point inside any of the allowlist roots (%USERPROFILE%, %TEMP%, %TMP%, %LACERTE_DATA_ROOT% — %TEMP% is the easiest, since it's user-write by definition) can redirect the wire log to a sensitive location. Example: `mklink /J %TEMP%\lac-logs C:\Users\victim\Documents\Personal` (junction, no admin needed), then set `LACERTE_DEBUG_WIRE=1` and `LACERTE_DEBUG_LOG_PATH=%TEMP%\lac-logs` in the MCP host config (or in env an attacker controls). PathValidation accepts the path: literal canonical form is under %TEMP%, no `..`, no UNC, no control chars — `Path.GetFullPath` on .NET Framework 4.8 does NOT follow reparse points, so the canonical string is still `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Temp\lac-logs`. WireLog.WriteRecord then calls `Directory.CreateDirectory(cfg.LogDir)` (which traverses the junction) and writes the log file containing operator-visible diagnostics + wire-scope-redacted but Disk-scope-broad PII through the junction to `C:\Users\victim\Documents\Personal`. The on-disk log carries the full broad-keyset content (rawError, reason, Description redacted, but everything else passes the disk-scope redactor).
description: Verified at src/LacertMCP.Server/Session/PathValidation.cs:200-202: `try { canonical = Path.GetFullPath(logDir); } catch { return null; }`. `Path.GetFullPath` documentation explicitly does NOT resolve symbolic links or NTFS junctions — it does syntactic canonicalization only (collapse `.`/`..`, resolve relative paths, normalize separators). The allowlist check at line 228-232 (`pathWithSep.StartsWith(rootCanonical)`) operates on the syntactic canonical, so a junction at %TEMP%\anything that points outside the allowlist roots passes. The threat is realizable today on Windows without admin rights — `mklink /J` (directory junction) only needs write access to the parent. The dataPath path (ValidateDataPath, line 54-158) has the same structural gap but is less exposed: LACERTE_DATA_ROOT is operator-set and the dataPath comes through `lacerte_set_context` which the operator drives; the LACERTE_DEBUG_LOG_PATH path is set once in the MCP host config and the log file gets PII content automatically thereafter. P15-019 / P15-001 split the redaction scopes for exactly this 'logs may leave the host' threat — but the redactor only matters if the file lands at the expected path.
recommendation: Resolve the canonical path AFTER following reparse points before applying the allowlist check. On net48, the cleanest path is `new DirectoryInfo(canonical).Exists` to verify, then `GetFinalPathNameByHandle` via P/Invoke to resolve all junctions/symlinks to the actual target (or for a simpler alternative, refuse to write into a directory whose `DirectoryInfo.Attributes & FileAttributes.ReparsePoint` is set on any segment from the allowlist root downward). Minimal fix: after `Path.GetFullPath`, walk parent directories from the allowlist root to the leaf and reject if any segment has the ReparsePoint attribute — this catches both symlinks and junctions without the P/Invoke. Add the same guard to ValidateDataPath for symmetry. Test: create a junction under a temp test dir, point ValidateLogDir at it, assert it returns null. Cost: ~30 LoC including the segment walk + tests.
rationale: Grep of all three audit JSONs for `symlink|junction|reparse|GetFullPath.*resolve` returns no prior finding. The round-4 brief explicitly asks 'LACERTE_DEBUG_LOG_PATH: any path validation, or attacker-controlled redirect?' — the answer is 'yes, validated' but the validation has this specific syntactic-vs-semantic-canonical gap. The threat model in the brief (`attacker = anyone in the process's env. Could redirect LACERTE_DEBUG_LOG_PATH to e.g. /Documents/personal/`) is exactly the realized attack: env-controlled value + allowlist that doesn't follow reparse points = the redirect succeeds even with the allowlist. P14-049 introduced the allowlist; no prior round modeled reparse-point bypass. Materially improves the worst case (debug log lands in attacker-chosen directory carrying broad-keyset disk-scope content) at small cost (single walker function, no API change).

verdict.reasoning:
Verified the code claim at C:/Users/VR/Projects/LacertMCP/src/LacertMCP.Server/Session/PathValidation.cs:200-234. ValidateLogDir does call Path.GetFullPath (line 201) and then applies StartsWith on the allowlist roots (line 229). On .NET Framework 4.8, Path.GetFullPath performs syntactic canonicalization only — it does NOT follow NTFS junctions or symlinks. The allowlist therefore operates on the literal path string, and a junction at e.g. %TEMP%\lac-logs pointing to C:\Users\<user>\Documents\Personal would pass: canonical string starts with %TEMP%, no ".." segments, no UNC, no control chars. Subsequent Directory.CreateDirectory + File.Open in WireLog would actually traverse the junction. mklink /J does not require admin (only write to parent); %TEMP% is user-writable by definition.

Novelty: grepped all three prior audit JSONs (audit-findings.json, audit-findings-r2.json, audit-findings-r3.json) for symlink|junction|reparse|ReparsePoint|GetFinalPathName — zero matches. P14-049 introduced the allowlist (cited in r1 finding 1060) and was explicitly about path-string validation but did not model semantic-vs-syntactic canonicalization. P15-019 split redaction scopes for the "logs may leave the host" threat. Both prior investments are circumvented by this gap. No prior round flagged the reparse-point bypass.

Materiality: The project explicitly invested across multiple rounds in this exact security boundary (env-controlled log path → allowlist → scope-split redactor), and this gap defeats those investments at the lowest layer. The disk-scope log payload (WireLog.cs:23, 805) carries the broad keyset — secrets are redacted but operator-visible diagnostics + PII are not. Fix is small (~30 LoC: walk parent segments from allowlist root to leaf, reject if any has FileAttributes.ReparsePoint set; no P/Invoke needed) and consistent with the existing defensive posture. Caveat: single-operator personal tool per CLAUDE.md narrows the threat model — attacker needs both (a) ability to create files in user-writable %TEMP% (any local user) and (b) influence over MCP host env config. But defense-in-depth on a boundary the project already pays for is worth the small fix cost.

One minor refinement to the recommendation: also reject when LACERTE_DEBUG_LOG_PATH itself names a reparse-point directory (not just intermediate segments) — the segment walker should include the leaf.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Add a single helper in PathValidation.cs that walks segments from each allowlist root down to the candidate path's leaf and rejects if any segment's DirectoryInfo.Attributes carries FileAttributes.ReparsePoint. Call it from ValidateLogDir between line 228 (EnsureTrailingSeparator) and line 229 (allowlist StartsWith check) — only invoke when the path matched an allowlist root, so non-existent-yet directories under valid roots still pass on first write (the walker should stop at the first non-existent segment and treat that as clean — junctions can only exist on extant directories). Apply the same guard to ValidateDataPath for symmetry (lower exposure but same structural gap). Tests in SessionToolsTests.cs (or a new PathValidationTests): (a) create a real junction under a temp dir via cmd /c mklink /J on Windows, assert ValidateLogDir returns null; (b) regular subdirectory under temp root passes; (c) non-existent path under valid root passes (don't break the lazy-create flow); (d) skip the junction test on non-Windows via Skip attribute since mklink is Windows-only. Cost: ~30 LoC + 4 tests. No public API change. Document the threat model in the ValidateLogDir XML doc so future audits know reparse-point resistance is part of the contract.

title: Registration.GetStoredAppId and AppIdStore drift on `LACERTE_MCP_FORCE_FILE_STORE` semantics — sim-mode register on Windows stores to file but live-mode read still hits Credential Manager when the env var is later unset
userOrOpsImpact: An operator who ran `lacerte-mcp register` once with LACERTE_MCP_FORCE_FILE_STORE=1 set (a real path — the CI smoke / dev-on-Windows / multi-account-Windows recipe) will see register succeed (file written) — but then on the production MCP startup (env var unset) Registration.GetStoredAppId() looks at Credential Manager, finds nothing, returns null, and the session manager throws AppNotRegistered (9006). The operator's troubleshooting reads 'AppID not persisted; run `lacerte-mcp register`' — they re-run register, see it succeed, restart, get 9006 again. No surface tells them the storage backend silently switched between the two invocations.
description: AppIdStore.UsesCredentialManager (Cli/Storage/AppIdStore.cs:59) is read at every call AND honors LACERTE_MCP_FORCE_FILE_STORE=1. Registration.GetStoredAppId() (Server/Bridge/Registration.cs:117) also honors the env var. But neither side persists or surfaces a *witness* of which backend stored the last AppID. The two reads racing different env-var states across two process invocations — `lacerte-mcp register` with the var set, then `LacertMCP.Server.exe` startup without it — produce a silent split-brain: AppID exists in the file, but the live bridge looks at CredMan and reports 'absent', surfacing as 9006 AppNotRegistered. The doctor probe is wired to AppIdStore.GetDiagnostic() which uses the *current* process env (consistent with whatever invocation reads it), so doctor cannot diagnose the cross-process drift either. This is doubly cross-platform-relevant because on POSIX UsesCredentialManager is permanently false (no CredMan), so a developer who tests an MCP path on POSIX with the file backend, then ships the same registration data to a Windows operator, gets the same backend mismatch on the operator's first MCP startup.
recommendation: When AppIdStore.Set() writes the AppID, also write a tiny sentinel into the OTHER backend (a 'see file at: {path}' marker in CredMan, or a 'see CredMan' marker in the file) so a later GetStoredAppId from the 'wrong' backend can surface a precise 'AppID stored via file backend; this process is reading CredMan because LACERTE_MCP_FORCE_FILE_STORE is unset' error rather than the misleading 'absent'. Alternatively (cheaper): include the active backend in the doctor 'AppID GUID' probe Detail (current code already prints 'via Credential Manager' / 'via file' — extend it to surface BOTH locations' status: 'CredMan: absent / file: present (LACERTE_MCP_FORCE_FILE_STORE not set in current process)' so the diagnostic is unambiguous).
rationale: audit-findings-r2.json title 'LACERTE_APP_ID env var documented but ignored; only Credential Manager / file is read' covers env-var-vs-store confusion but not the cross-process backend-drift case. No prior finding examines what happens when LACERTE_MCP_FORCE_FILE_STORE differs between CLI register invocation and Server startup invocation. The Registration.cs comment 'Kept in sync with that file at the same target constant' (line 26) shows the maintainers already worry about this drift surface but only the constant is sync'd, not the backend-resolution logic.

verdict.reasoning:
VERIFIED. Code reads (Registration.cs:119, AppIdStore.cs:59-66) both consult LACERTE_MCP_FORCE_FILE_STORE from the CURRENT process env at every Get/Set call. Set() writes to whichever backend the env-var resolution selects at that moment; a later GetStoredAppId() in a different process inherits whatever env it has — there is no in-store witness telling the reader which backend the writer used. The split-brain scenario is real: CLI register with the var set writes to file; Server startup without the var reads CredMan, gets nothing, throws AppNotRegistered (9006). The doctor probe via AppIdStore.GetDiagnostic() runs in the doctor process's env so it CANNOT diagnose the cross-process mismatch — confirmed at AppIdStore.cs:128-158 (uses UsesCredentialManager which is current-process-bound).

NOVELTY: Confirmed novel against all 3 prior rounds. The closest neighbor R2-P15-005 (LACERTE_APP_ID env-var-vs-store) addressed env-as-source confusion but explicitly punted on alternate backend resolution — its accepted recommendation was option (b) "delete from .env.example, don't add env-var support" and never examined what happens when LACERTE_MCP_FORCE_FILE_STORE itself drifts across process invocations. R3-P16-013 addressed AppName drift between CLI literal defaults and server env reads — a different config surface. R3-P16-058 addressed doctor's AppID-Phase-9-stub remediation honesty — addressed the wrong NotSignedIn cause (stub consent ceremony), not the wrong NotSignedIn cause this finding flags (silent backend mismatch). R2-P15-076 zeroed byte[] residency in the same TryCredRead — unrelated mechanism. No prior finding examines cross-process drift on the FORCE_FILE_STORE knob specifically.

MATERIALLY IMPROVES: Yes, but narrowly. The operator population that hits this is small — LACERTE_MCP_FORCE_FILE_STORE is documented as "testing only" in R2's accepted recommendations (P15-005 and P14-016/P14-033). Realistic victims: (a) Windows devs sometimes running tests with the var set in a shell then forgetting to clear it before launching the MCP server, (b) multi-account-Windows operators who got mid-stream advice to use the var, (c) CI smoke that exports to a script but not to a launched server. The fix (extend doctor's AppID probe Detail to surface BOTH locations: "CredMan: absent / file: present (LACERTE_MCP_FORCE_FILE_STORE not set in this process)") is cheap, ~20 LOC, and aligns with the diagnostic-truth pattern already adopted in P16-058. Saves a real 30-60 minute troubleshooting session when it triggers. Confidence is medium because the user population is bounded and the env var is gated behind "testing only" framing — but the doctor-probe-extension cost-of-fix is low enough that the cost/benefit still favors landing it. Doctor's whole purpose is to surface exactly this class of silent config-resolution drift.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Take only the CHEAPER half of the original recommendation (skip the sentinel-cross-write idea — it creates a new persistence write side-effect and inverse drift problems). Single-file edit in C:/Users/VR/Projects/LacertMCP/src/LacertMCP.Cli/Commands/DoctorCommand.cs ProbeAppId:

(1) Add a small helper alongside AppIdStore that probes BOTH backends regardless of current env-var state. New static method `AppIdStore.GetDualBackendDiagnostic(out bool credManPresent, out bool filePresent, out string? credManRaw, out string? fileRaw)` that calls TryCredRead directly (Windows only — wrap in IsWindows check) and ReadRawFromFile() directly, ignoring UsesCredentialManager. Sim-safe; off-Windows credManPresent always false.

(2) In DoctorCommand.ProbeAppId Detail strings (both Absent and Ok branches), extend to surface BOTH locations. Example Absent on Windows: `"Detail: CredMan target 'lacerte-mcp': absent; %APPDATA%/lacerte-mcp/config.json: present (AppID minted via file backend — LACERTE_MCP_FORCE_FILE_STORE not set in this process so CredMan was checked instead). The doctor-probe-only fix achieves the same diagnostic outcome at 1/5 the surface-area cost.

Also explicitly call this out in DECISIONS.md as a one-line addendum to the existing 2026-05-30 "AppID GUID in Windows Credential Manager" entry: `"LACERTE_MCP_FORCE_FILE_STORE is a per-process toggle; the AppID written by one process is NOT migrated to the other backend when the toggle differs. Doctor surfaces both backends' presence to make the drift visible — see DoctorCommand.ProbeAppId."`
